description:
The Construction of Fish Markets scheme is an initiative launched by the Government of India to enhance the infrastructure for the fishery sector. 

This scheme was officially launched on December 18, 2020. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to improve the marketing infrastructure for fish and fish products. 

The government aims to construct modern fish markets across various coastal states in India. 

These markets are intended to provide better facilities for fish farmers and fishermen. 

The initiative seeks to increase the income of fishers and improve their livelihoods. 

The scheme also aims to ensure that consumers have access to fresh and quality fish products. 

The targeted beneficiaries of this scheme include local fishermen, fish farmers, and fish vendors. 

The government has set a goal to construct at least 500 fish markets across the country. 

Each fish market is expected to be equipped with modern amenities. 

These amenities include cold storage facilities, auction halls, and retail spaces. 

The estimated cost for constructing each fish market is around INR 1 crore. 

The total budget allocated for this scheme is approximately INR 500 crores. 

The implementation of this scheme is expected to create job opportunities in the fishery sector. 

It is projected that around 50,000 jobs will be generated through this initiative. 

The scheme also aims to promote sustainable fishing practices among local communities. 

The eligibility criteria for beneficiaries include being a registered fisherman or fish farmer. 

There are no specific age limits set for eligibility under this scheme. 

However, beneficiaries must demonstrate a commitment to sustainable fishing practices. 

The application process for this scheme involves several steps. 

Interested beneficiaries must first register with the local fisheries department. 

They are required to submit an application form along with necessary documents. 

These documents typically include proof of identity, proof of occupation, and proof of registration as a fisherman or fish farmer. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the local fisheries department. 

If approved, the beneficiaries will receive a notification regarding the construction of the fish market. 

The timeline for the construction of each fish market is approximately 6 to 12 months. 

Disbursement of funds for the construction is typically done in phases. 

The first phase involves the release of 30 percent of the total budget upon project approval. 

Subsequent disbursements are made based on the progress of construction. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

The local fisheries departments in various states are responsible for execution. 

Contact details for the Ministry can be found on their official website. 

The scheme is part of the larger initiative to boost the blue economy in India. 

The blue economy refers to the sustainable use of ocean resources for economic growth. 

The government has recognized the potential of the fishery sector in contributing to the economy. 

India is the second-largest fish producer in the world, contributing to about 7.5 percent of global fish production. 

The fishery sector provides direct employment to around 14 million people in India. 

The construction of fish markets is expected to enhance the supply chain for fish products. 

This will help reduce post-harvest losses, which currently stand at around 20 to 30 percent. 

The scheme also aims to promote the export of fish and fish products. 

India's fish exports were valued at approximately INR 46,000 crores in the fiscal year 2020-2021. 

The government aims to increase this figure significantly through improved infrastructure. 

The scheme is expected to benefit not only fishermen but also consumers. 

Consumers will have access to fresher fish at competitive prices. 

The construction of fish markets will also help in maintaining hygiene standards. 

Each market will be designed to meet specific health and safety regulations. 

The government has partnered with various stakeholders for the successful implementation of this scheme. 

These stakeholders include local self-governments, cooperative societies, and non-governmental organizations. 

Training programs will also be conducted for fishermen and fish vendors. 

These programs will focus on best practices in fish handling and marketing. 

The government is committed to monitoring the progress of the scheme regularly. 

Periodic assessments will be conducted to ensure that the objectives are being met. 

Feedback from beneficiaries will also be taken into account for future improvements. 

The Construction of Fish Markets scheme is a significant step towards enhancing the fishery sector in India. 

It reflects the government's commitment to improving the livelihoods of fishermen. 

The scheme is expected to contribute to the overall economic development of coastal regions. 

By providing better infrastructure, the government aims to empower local communities. 

This initiative is aligned with the broader goals of the National Fisheries Policy. 

The National Fisheries Policy was launched in 2020 to promote sustainable development in the sector. 

The government has also introduced various other schemes to support the fishery sector. 

These include the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana and the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund. 

Together, these initiatives aim to create a robust framework for the growth of the fishery sector in India. 

The Construction of Fish Markets scheme is a crucial component of this framework. 

It is expected to pave the way for a more organized and efficient fish market system. 

This will ultimately benefit the economy and the livelihoods of millions of people involved in fishing.
